# Debunking claim Fauci co-authored paper saying masks caused most Spanish flu deaths

## The paper is real, but it doesn't say masks caused millions of deaths during the pandemic.

### Published Aug. 10, 2026

**Image courtesy of @mykolasosiukin and Bill Clark, accessed via Canva.com and Getty Images, illustrated by Snopes**

Claim:

Dr. Anthony Fauci co-authored a paper that found masks caused most deaths during the 1918 Spanish flu pandemic.

In late July and early August 2026, social media users recirculated a rumor that Dr. Anthony Fauci, the former director of the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, stated in a scientific paper that face masks caused most deaths during the Spanish flu pandemic in the early 20th century.

For example, on July 30, one Facebook user shared an image (archived) featuring text that claimed Fauci co-authored a paper in 2008 that found "most of the victims of the Spanish Flu didn't die" from the illness but instead "died from bacterial pneumonia ... caused by ... wearing masks." The Facebook user questioned why the physician, who helped lead the U.S. government's COVID-19 response, "knew" this but still "recommended mask mandates."

**(Facebook user John C. Sims)**

The claim recirculated primarily on Facebook. Snopes readers also contacted us to ask whether Fauci had published such a finding.

Though he did co-author a paper examining the role of bacterial pneumonia in deaths during the Spanish flu pandemic, the paper did not conclude that masks caused those infections. In fact, it did not discuss masks at all. Fauci also reportedly directly rejected the claim when the Associated Press asked him about it in 2023 (archived). As such, we have rated this claim false.

We first investigated versions of this rumor in October 2020.

## What does Fauci's 2008 paper actually say?

The paper at the center of the rumor is real. It is titled, "Predominant Role of Bacterial Pneumonia as a Cause of Death in Pandemic Influenza: Implications for Pandemic Influenza Preparedness." It was published on Oct. 1, 2008 (not 2009, as the above Facebook user claimed), in "The Journal of Infectious Diseases."

The researchers examined lung tissue obtained during 58 autopsies of people who died during the Spanish flu pandemic. They also reviewed pathologic and bacteriologic data from 109 published reports that included 8,398 individual autopsies. They concluded that the majority of deaths during the pandemic "likely resulted directly from secondary bacterial pneumonia" caused by bacteria commonly found in the upper respiratory tract.

The team did not conclude that masks caused those bacterial infections, as social media posts claimed. Searches for "masks" or "face coverings" on the page returned no results and the researchers made no connection between wearing masks and bacterial pneumonia.

An August 2008 news release regarding the study further explains how the bacterial pneumonia developed. Fauci said the evidence favored a scenario in which "viral damage followed by bacterial pneumonia led to the vast majority of deaths," adding that "the virus landed the first blow while bacteria delivered the knockout punch." The news release reads, in part:

> The majority of deaths during the influenza pandemic of 1918-1919 were not caused by the influenza virus acting alone, report researchers from the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID), part of the National Institutes of Health.
One caption reads, “Here is the Dr Fauci article from 2008 saying that most deaths from the 1918 Spanish Flu were caused by Bacterial pneumonia!
Anthony Fauci "wrote a paper regarding the Spanish Flu and stated that the majority of deaths in 1918-1919 was because of bacterial pneumonia ...
Anthony Fauci showed that “most of the deaths” during the 1918-1919 Spanish flu pandemic were actually due to infections from face masks. AP'S ...
by DM Morens · 2008 · Cited by 2275 — ... 1918–1919 pandemic), histological and bacteriologic evidence suggests that the vast majority of influenza deaths resulted from secondary bacterial pneumonia.

# The Infodemic: Dr. Fauci Didn't Write Paper Blaming Most Spanish Flu Deaths on Masks

* By Polygraph

October 22, 2020 3:22 PM

The Infodemic: Dr. Fauci Didn't Write Paper Blaming Most Spanish Flu Deaths on Masks

FILE - Dr. Anthony Fauci, director of the National Institute for Allergy and Infectious Diseases, speaks on Capitol Hill in Washington, July 31, 2020. (Kevin Dietsch/Pool via AP)

*Fake news about the coronavirus can do real harm. Polygraph.info is spotlighting fact-checks from other reliable sources here.*

### **Daily Debunk**

**Claim:** Dr. Anthony Fauci "wrote a paper regarding the Spanish Flu and stated that the majority of deaths in 1918-1919 was because of bacterial pneumonia from wearing masks."

**Verdict:** False

**Read the full story at:** Politifact.com

**Social Media Disinfo**

**Fact check:** "Social media users have claimed that a document from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) admits that the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which is the name for the novel coronavirus, does not exist. While the document is authentic, the scientific process described within it has been misrepresented." -- Reuters Fact Check

**Verdict:** False

**Read the full story at:** Reuters.com/fact-check

### **Factual Reads on Coronavirus**

**China's Covid success compared to Europe shows lockdowns are a first step, not a solution**  
As much of Europe stares down the barrel of renewed coronavirus lockdowns, and a potentially miserable -- and deadly --winter to come, China is going from strength to strength.  
-- CNN, October 19

**The coronavirus test results that predict an outbreak's course**  
Viral levels in people infected with SARS-CoV-2 in a specific town or city could be used to assess whether the epidemic there has passed its peak.  
-- Nature, October 19

**Eight Persistent COVID-19 Myths and Why People Believe Them**  
From a human-made virus to vaccine conspiracy theories, we rounded up the most insidious false claims about the pandemic  
-- Scientific American, October 12

**5 Things to Know About a COVID Vaccine: It Won’t Be a ‘Magic Wand’**  
President Donald Trump makes no secret he would like a COVID-19 vaccine to be available before the election. But it’s doubtful that will happen.  
-- Kaiser Health News, October 5

**Watch: Antibodies, immunity, and what they mean for Covid-19, explained**  
The immune system is no wimp. When pathogens cause illness, it kicks into high gear. Cells work together to tag, kill and gobble up invaders as they fight the infection.  
-- Stat, May 5

**The race for coronavirus vaccines: a graphical guide**  
Eight ways in which scientists hope to provide immunity to SARS-CoV-2.  
-- Nature, April 28
